newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN - Rwandan Hutus said heading for C.Africa, Angola.
newsitem.headline: UN - Rwandan Hutus said heading for C.Africa, Angola.

text.p: The United Nations refugee agency UNHCR quoted unconfirmed Zairean reports on Tuesday as saying 65,000 Rwandan refugees, among them former soldiers, were heading for neighbouring Central African republic to the north.
Spokeswoman Pamela O'Toole also said UNHCR had unconfirmed reports of another 30,000 refugees, among them big numbers of young men, moving towards the Angolan border to the south.
UNHCR planned to send teams to the region to check the reported refugee movements, both in territory still controlled by Zaire's government troops, she told a briefing.
It was the first reported spotting of the Hutus since they fled Tingi-Tingi camp in March, when rebels fighting to topple cancer-stricken leader Mobutu Sese Seko captured it.

O'Toole said Zairean military and local sources reported spotting 65,000 Rwandan Hutus at Ikela and Bokungu areas in government-controlled territory southwest of the regional eastern capital Kisangani, seized by the rebels in mid-March.

In reports which UNHCR could not confirm independently, the Zairean sources told the agency the refugees were heading for the Central African Republic, possibly through Mbandaka, a Zairean border town on the Congo river, O'Toole said.
There were reports that members of Rwanda's former Hutu government army were among the refugees, O'Toole added.

The Rwandan refugees fled to eastern Zaire fearing reprisals for the 1994 Hutu-led genocide of more than half a million minority Tutsis and moderate Hutus in Rwanda. With every rumoured rebel attack, they have fled deeper into Zaire.
